analysis:
The change is confined to provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Inference/Engine/ProductionModelCalibrationTests.swift, a test-only file with no production code. It adds a private helper, requireEngineIdle (head lines 308-318), which polls engine.capacity().activeRequests and budget.serviceBudget.count until both reach 0, with a 10s deadline. It replaces the immediate idle assertions at head lines 45, 68, 118, 146, 219 and 257, and adds one at 253. The helper only reads engine capacity gauges and the budget count and adds a bounded poll. It adds no new I/O, secrets, network paths or crypto changes, and does not weaken any production control.

Threat-model relevance is limited. T-041 and TB-007 cover the prefix cache and inference engine, but the tests run with PrefixCachePolicy.environmentFlag set to "0" (head line 358), so SSD cache behavior is not exercised or altered. The test fixtures still assert that calibration performs no customer work (productionCalibrationWorkCounters == [0,0,0,0]) and that service-budget charges are released, which preserves resource-leak coverage. The new wait tolerates the engine republishing its capacity gauges after the terminal event. Because it polls with a 10s timeout and fails hard via #require, it still catches a genuine leak of active requests or budget charges.

One minor test-quality note: the idle checks at lines 118 and 146 are placed before the decodeRowsTotal assertions. This is a deterministic-ordering improvement. I found no security regression and no required threat-model update. No production source was changed, so there are no remaining integration questions.
